ūna: ūna (adj.) [Vedic ūna; cp. Av. ūna, Gr. eu)_nis, Lat. vāpus, Goth. wans, Ags. won = E. want] wanting, deficient, less M II.73; J V.330; DhA I.77; DhA IV.210. Mostly adverbially with numerals = one less, but one, minus (one or two); usually with eka (as ekūna one less, e. g. ekūna--aṭṭhasataṃ (799) J I.57; ekūna--pañcasate KhA 91, ekūna--vīsati (19) Vism 287; ekenɔūnesu pañcasu attabhāvasatesu (499) J I.167; also with eka in instr. as eken"ūnapañcasatāni (deficient by one) Vin II.285; KhA 91; sometimes without eka, e. g. ūnapañcasatāni (499) Vin III.284; ūnavīsati (19) Vin IV.130, 148. With "two" less: dvīhi ūnaṃ sahassaṃ (998) J I.255. -- anūna not deficient, complete PvA 285 (= paripuṇṇa). --udara (ūnudara, ūnūdara, ūnodara) an empty stomach, adj. Qof empty stomach; °udara J II.293; VI.295; °ūdara J VI.258; Miln 406; odara Sn 707; DhA I.170. --bhāva depletion, deficiency SnA 463 (v. l. hānabhāva).
ūnaka: ūnaka (adj.) [ūna + ka] deficient, wanting, lacking Vin III.81, 254; IV.263; Sn 721; Miln 310, 311, (°satta--vassika one who is not yet 7 years old), 414; DhA I.79.
ūnatta: ūnatta (nt.) [abstr. fr. ūna] depletion, deficiency Vin II. 239; J V.450.
